modules.title: Lesson 1: The Meaning of Salvation
modules.description: Understand sin, God's redemptive plan, and salvation by grace through the finished work of Christ.
modules.introduction: Salvation means rescue, deliverance, and restoration from sin through Jesus Christ. It is not merely joining a church, moral reform, or a ritual.

lessons.title: Sin and its consequences
lessons.content: Sin is disobedience, rebellion, and independence from God. It separates people from God, corrupts human life, and brings judgment. Salvation begins by acknowledging our need for God's mercy.

lessons.title: God's redemptive plan in Christ
lessons.content: God's plan was not an afterthought. The Old Testament points toward a Redeemer. Jesus is fully God and fully human, lived without sin, died as a substitute, and rose again. His work is complete.

lessons.title: Grace, faith, and transformed life
lessons.content: Salvation is received by grace through faith, not earned by works. Good works follow salvation as its fruit. Ask candidates to explain the Gospel and their personal response to Christ.

discussionQuestions: Why is salvation more than joining a church?
How does understanding sin deepen gratitude for grace?
Why must salvation be by grace and not works?
reviewQuestions: What is sin and what are its consequences?
assignments: Read Ephesians 2:8–10 and summarize the relationship between grace, faith, and good works.
Prepare a brief personal testimony of your response to Christ.
modules.conclusion: Salvation is God's rescue plan accomplished through Jesus Christ, received by grace through faith, and evidenced by a transformed life.

modules.title: Lesson 2: Repentance
modules.description: Understand repentance as an essential Gospel response: a Spirit-produced change of heart and a turn toward God.
scriptureReferences: Mark 1:14–15; Luke 24:47; Acts 2:38; Acts 17:30; 2 Corinthians 7:9–10; Acts 26:20
modules.introduction: Repentance is not an optional emotional response. Jesus and the apostles preached it as a central part of the Gospel call.

lessons.title: The meaning and necessity of repentance
lessons.content: Metanoia describes a change of mind and heart that turns a person from sin toward God. Repentance is necessary because sin is universal, serious, and contrary to God's holiness.

lessons.title: Godly sorrow and true turning
lessons.content: Worldly sorrow grieves consequences without transformation. Godly sorrow leads to confession, forsaking sin, and a new direction of obedience.

lessons.title: The fruit of repentance
lessons.content: Conviction, confession, turning from sin, and turning to God are followed by visible fruit such as obedience, restitution where possible, and new patterns of righteousness. Repentance prepares the heart for baptism.

discussionQuestions: What is the difference between regret and repentance?
Why is repentance necessary for baptismal candidates?
What fruit might demonstrate a changed direction?
reviewQuestions: What does repentance mean in the Gospel?
Name two fruits of genuine repentance.
assignments: Read 2 Corinthians 7:9–10 and write how godly sorrow differs from regret.
Identify one area where you need to turn toward God and seek support from a trusted leader.
modules.conclusion: Repentance is a Spirit-produced turning from sin toward God. It is the doorway into Christian life and prepares the heart for baptism.

modules.title: Lesson 3: Faith in Jesus Christ
modules.description: Understand saving faith as personal trust in the person and finished work of Jesus Christ.
modules.introduction: If repentance turns from sin, faith turns to Christ. Saving faith is the means by which salvation is received; it is not merely agreement that God exists.

lessons.title: The nature and object of saving faith
lessons.content: Saving faith includes knowing the Gospel, agreeing that it is true, and personally trusting Christ. Its object is Jesus, not a church, pastor, religious system, or personal goodness.

lessons.title: Confession and lordship
lessons.content: Romans 10 connects belief in the heart with confession by the mouth. Receiving Jesus as Savior includes acknowledging His authority and responding in obedience.

lessons.title: Assurance through Christ
lessons.content: Assurance rests on God's promise, Christ's finished work, the Spirit's witness, and a transformed life. Works confirm faith; they do not earn salvation.

discussionQuestions: What is the difference between intellectual agreement and personal trust?
Why is Jesus the only object of saving faith?
How do good works relate to salvation?
reviewQuestions: What are the three dimensions of saving faith?
What are the foundations of assurance?
assignments: Read Romans 10:9–10 and write a short statement describing your trust in Christ.
Prepare to share why you are choosing baptism as a public confession of faith.
modules.conclusion: Saving faith is wholehearted trust in the crucified and risen Christ that leads to surrender, transformation, and confident assurance.

modules.title: Lesson 4: The New Birth (Regeneration)
modules.description: Understand why regeneration is necessary and what it means to be born again.
modules.introduction: Humanity's problem is not only behavior but spiritual death. Jesus told Nicodemus that a person must be born again to see the kingdom of God.

lessons.title: The necessity and meaning of new birth
lessons.content: Regeneration is a supernatural act of God that gives spiritual life to a spiritually dead person. It is not church membership, moral improvement, water baptism, or an emotional experience.

lessons.title: The new nature and ongoing growth
lessons.content: The new birth creates a new heart and a capacity for obedience. Believers still experience conflict between flesh and Spirit, but new life produces a changed relationship with sin and a desire for righteousness.

lessons.title: Evidence and baptism
lessons.content: Love for God, desire for Scripture, growth, and perseverance are signs of new life. The Spirit regenerates; water baptism testifies outwardly to the inward work of God.

discussionQuestions: Why is religion or morality not enough to replace regeneration?
What evidence of new life can a believer look for?
How does water baptism relate to the new birth?
reviewQuestions: Name two signs of new spiritual life.
assignments: Read John 3:1–10 and summarize what Jesus teaches about new birth.
Write down one way your desires or conduct have changed since trusting Christ.
modules.conclusion: The new birth is spiritual resurrection, not cosmetic change. Baptism declares the new life God has already begun.
